ghost_comments.analysis: The @tgtanalytics account shows a clear concentration of engagement in a single pinned post about local LLM hardware. That post accounts for 61% of the total score (18.85 of 31.0), driven primarily by 2 replies (weight 5.0 each). The remaining 6 posts averaged just 1.86 score, with 4 of them scoring below 1.0 — essentially invisible. The Jevons effect post was the second strongest at 6.55, powered by a repost and 3 likes, suggesting technical deep-dive content with concrete numbers resonates. Views are low across the board (16-97 per post), indicating the algorithm is not amplifying this account to new audiences. The follower-to-following ratio (154:327) is inverted, which limits discoverability.
recommendations: Double down on the format that worked: the pinned post was a thread-style technical analysis with real dollar figures. Replicate this for other hardware/AI topics — the data shows replies are worth 10x a like, so content that invites discussion (questions, comparisons, contrarian takes) will compound.
The Jevons/AI cost post got organic reposts and likes without any replies — it was shareable but not conversational. Mix shareable posts with discussion-bait posts to capture both signal types.

4 of 7 posts scored under 1.0 with zero engagement signals. These are dead weight in the feed. Consider deleting or pinning higher-quality posts, and reduce posting frequency to concentrate engagement on fewer, stronger posts.
ghost_comments.next_action: Write a follow-up thread expanding on the Strix Halo workstation analysis — same format (real numbers, hardware comparison, cost analysis), but end with a specific question to invite replies. Replies are the highest-weight signal at 5.0x and the account has proven it can earn them.
